messages:
maya: Heads up — saw regressions in the paged-attn path when FlashAttention v3 is active in canary-nyc (dedicated-4gpu). Repro + quick numbers below.

maya: Repro command i used:```bash
./bench --model star-7b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kernel flashv3 --paged
```

ben: Repro'd locally on canary. Short summary: seq <= 1024 is fine. For seq >= 2048 p95 latency jumps from ~120ms to ~220ms, p99 from ~240ms to ~480ms. Memory transient +30% and we've seen a couple OOM-retries on the canary pool.

ashley: :eyes: interesting — that smells like kv-page churn combined with a different allocation pattern in FAv3. Any flamegraphs/profiles?

perf-bot: profile: https://perf.redwood/internal/bench/1768549999 (flame + alloc snapshots).

ben: Flame shows a big hotspot in `paged_attn::page_fetch` when kernel=flashv3 — increased CPU time waiting on page-reads and a higher GC/alloc tail. Also saw more frequent small CUDA memcopies compared to FAv2.

li: Hypothesis: FAv3's fused kernels change chunking which increases simultaneous outstanding KV page reads for long sequences, causing scheduler contention and backpressure -> higher latency + memory spikes.

ashley: Agreed. Two mitigations we can try quickly: 1) temporary fflag to limit FAv3 to short/medium sequences, 2) a paged-fallback that switches to FAv2 (or unfused) for seq > threshold.

maya: Proposal: add two flags: `attn.flash_v3_seq_limit` (default 1536 in canary) and `attn.paged_fallback_enabled` (default true for canary). Also adjust batching heuristics for FAv3: prefer max_batch <= 8 for flashv3 when seq>1024 and shrink batching window from 20ms -> 8ms for those requests.

ben: I'll run a quick A/B: enable seq_limit=1536 on canary and turn on paged_fallback for long seq; measure p95/p99 over 30m. If numbers look good, we gate the flags to canary and then roll.

ashley: For the KV side i can try relaxing evict aggression: increase `kv.page_retain_ms` and add a small jitter to page writebacks to avoid synchronized bursts. Also instrument `kv.pending_reads` histograms.

li: Minor note: we should also add a safety auto-rollback in the rollout job if p99 increases by >20% vs baseline. Can we hook that into the canary job?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started at 1768550100. Jobs: deploy-canary-nyc-4gpu. Auto-rollback enabled: threshold = +20% p99.

ben: Quick numbers after flags applied (10m sample): p95 down to ~130ms, p99 ~260ms — still slightly higher than baseline but within rollback threshold. Memory stabilised, no OOMs in last 12m.

maya: Good signal. Next steps: ben open INF ticket with bench data + perf links (INF-1297). ashley iterate KV tune and add `kv.pending_reads` metric. li add the fflags to the rollout plan and a canary-only constraint. I'll follow up with a short runbook for ops in case we see thrash.

ben: Filed INF-1297 and added the bench logs + flamegraphs. Assigning to ashley and li.

ashley: on it. I’ll push a KV patch to canary tomorrow morning and post a short smoke report.

maya: Thanks team. If anyone sees regressions drop @maya and we’ll roll back the flag. :thumbsup:
